name: Rock Goblin
body:
Endemic to deep subterranean caverns and mountain dens, these cousins to goblins and hobgoblins are known for their ability to blend into the rocky terrain. Their favorite tactic is to ambush travelers, attacking them with crude clubs and axes, as well as fierce, gnashing bites from their rock-hard teeth.

Physical

Rock goblins are squat, round goblinoids, pudgy yet muscular. They are hairless and have bumpy skin that naturally resembles stone. They have red eyes and long, thin pointed ears. Their wide mouths are full of hard teeth, including two prominent canine fangs. They typically wear little clothing, relying on their rock-like skin to camouflage them and protect them from harm.

Social

Rock goblins are most common deep in the heart of Subterranea, although some do live in rocky areas on the surface, especially in mountains or badlands. They prefer to dwell in natural caves and canyons where they can take advantage of the unworked stone to use their camouflage ability.

Rock goblins prefer to attack by ambush, using stealth to take travelers by surprise.

For this reason, they rarely wear armor, relying instead on their natural armor and the element of surprise. They are incredibly tough and also ruthless, usually fighting to the death.

Rock goblins don’t take prisoners and don’t usually eat their enemies, but they take immense pleasure in bloodshed. They will chase down anyone who tries to escape just for the pleasure of another kill. If rock goblins don’t obtain enough supplies from banditry, or if they have not gotten their fill of violence, they will go on raids of nearby settlements. These raids inevitably end in murder sprees, sometimes reducing entire villages to ghost towns. Rock goblins may set up temporary bases in the ruins of villages they have conquered, but will eventually be forced to move along when their supplies run low.

Rock goblins are poorly organized. They love to swarm their targets, causing chaos and confusion, but they are poor at actually coordinating these attacks. Rock goblin bands are usually small, and will divide and go their separate ways if their numbers grow too large, so that the demand for resources is not too severe.

Rock goblins are omnivorous. They eat large quantities of fungi and minerals to supplement their diets, but prefer meat when they can get it. They rarely put the effort into raising their own food, preferring to hunt, gather, and steal what they need.

Alignment And Religion

Rock goblins are usually Chaotic Evil. They love cruelty and bloodshed, and delight in the fact that they are tougher than many other creatures. The average rock goblin is a malicious simpleton who would bludgeon an animal to death just to watch it die.

Most rock goblins worship the same pantheon of deities and demigods worshiped by goblins and their kin.

However, a fair number of them also belong to the Volcano Cults, who venerate evil Elemental Lords of Earth, Fire, and Magma.

Core Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are exceptionally durable, but lacking in mental capabilities. Your ability score modifiers are +4 Con, –2 Int, –2 Wis, –2 Cha [paragon]. (1)
Size As a Small creature, you have a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a +1 size bonus to your Armor Class, a –1 size penalty to your CMB, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks. You must use smaller weapons than Medium creatures. As a Small creature, you occupy a space of 5 feet by 5 feet. Your reach is 5 feet. (0)
Type You are a Humanoid with the goblinoid subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 20 feet. (–1)
Languages You begin play speaking Goblin and Undercommon. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Common, Draconic, Dwarven, Gnome, Ignan, Orc, and Terran. (0)
Other Traits
Bite You can make a bite attack with your rock-hard teeth. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d3 damage. (2)
Camouflage You gain a +4 species bonus on Stealth checks in naturally rocky terrain, whether above or below ground. (1)
Darkvision You have darkvision 60 feet. (2)
Natural Armor Your skin is as hard as stone, providing you with a +2 natural armor bonus to AC. (3)
Stone in the Blood You gain a +2 species bonus to saving throws against poison, paralysis, petrification, and polymorph effects. (2)
Total: 10 RP (standard)
Alternate Traits
Hardened Fists You can make two slam attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d3 bludgeoning damage each. This trait replaces bite.
Impervious You gain resistance 5 to both acid and fire. This trait replaces stone in the blood.
Inner Fire (Su) The magma that flows through the earth is somehow tied to the blood that courses through your veins. Once per day as a swift action, you can call on this elemental power to shroud your arms fire. Unarmed strikes with your elbows or hands, or attacks with weapons held in those hands, deal +1d6 points of fire damage. This lasts for 1 round per character level, although you may end the effects early as a free action. This trait replaces stone in the blood.
Plated Exoskeleton Your skin isn’t just hard, it’s covered in thick, overlapping stony plates. You receive a +5 natural armor bonus to AC. However, because of the great bulk of your exoskeleton, you have a difficult time wearing armor, even if you have the appropriate feat. All armor is treated as being one class bulkier than normal for you: treat light armor as medium armor, and medium armor as heavy armor. You cannot wear heavy armor. Regardless of the kind of armor worn, you suffer an additional –2 armor check penalty, +10% arcane spell failure chance, and your maximum Dexterity bonus is reduced by 2 (to a minimum of 0). This trait replaces natural armor.
Stability You receive a +4 species bonus to your CMD when resisting bull rush or trip attempts while standing on the ground. This trait replaces camouflage.
Stonesinger You are treated as 1 level higher when casting spells with the earth descriptor or using powers of the Earth domain, bloodline powers of the earth elemental bloodline, and revelations of the oracle’s stone mystery. This trait does not give you early access to level-based powers; it only affects powers you could already use without this trait. This trait replaces stone in the blood.
Stony Step You gain Stony Step as a bonus feat at 1st level. You count as an oread for this feat and for any feat that lists Stony Step as a prerequisite. This trait replaces camouflage and stone in the blood.
Subterranean Stalker You are more agile and perceptive than most rock goblins, but you are still just as dim-witted and offputting. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Con, –2 Int, –2 Cha. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Tremorsense You have learned to detect the slightest vibration in the earth around you. You gain tremorsense B1 with a range of 30 feet. This trait replaces camouflage and stone in the blood.
Weapon Familiarity You are proficient with the greatclub and the greataxe, and you treat any weapon with the word “goblin” in its name as a martial weapon. This trait replaces stone in the blood.
Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add +1/2 to acid damage or fire damage dealt by your bombs.
Barbarian Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls for attacks made with unarmed strikes or natural weapons (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Brawler Add +1/4 to your effective brawler level to determine your unarmed strike damage.
Cleric Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Druid Add +1/3 to your natural armor bonus when using wild shape.
Fighter Add +1 to the fighter’s CMD when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt.
Monk Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a trip attempt and +1/3 to the number of stunning attacks you can attempt per day.
Ranger Add +1/4 to your favored terrain for Mountain, Underground, or Urban. You must have the selected favored terrain to select this option.
Rogue Add a +1 bonus on your sneak attack damage rolls during the surprise round or before the target has acted in combat.
Slayer Add a +1/2 bonus on Perception checks while in rocky terrain.
Sorcerer Choose acid or fire damage. Add +1/2 point of the chosen energy damage to sorcerer spells you cast that deal the chosen energy damage.
Summoner Add a +1/4 natural armor bonus to the AC of your eidolon.
Warpriest Add +1/2 to the number of times per day you can use blessings, but these additional uses can be from only the Destruction, Earth, Earthquake, Fire, and Trickery blessings.
Witch Add +1 spell from the witch spell list to your familiar. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level witch spell you can cast. If you ever replace your familiar, the new familiar knows these bonus spells.
